The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan, has warned political parties and their supporters against turning the 2027 general elections into a battlefield, urging them to embrace peaceful campaigns and respect the rights of other political actors. Amupitan said rising cases of political violence, attacks on party members and intimidation of citizens could undermine the credibility of the elections before voting begins. He spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at a high-level security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, with leaders of political parties and other stakeholders ahead of the 2027 elections. The INEC chairman, who disclosed that the commission suspended its meeting to attend the engagement, described the situation as worrying. He said, “If I tell you that as Chair of INEC I’m not concerned, I’m worried about the state of violence and thuggery, attacks on Nigerian citizens, on political party members who we’re supposed to work with, then I’ll be deceiving everybody. It’s a worrying situation.” Amupitan recalled that he had previously urged political leaders not to turn elections into a battlefield but an opportunity for parties to present their policies and ideas to voters. “You will recall during my address to the leaders of the political parties and members of the National Peace Committee on the 18th of August 2026, I emphasised one very key point, that we should not turn our election into a battlefield, but as we proceed with campaigns, that we should look at the election as a competitive interviewing job,” he said. He argued that political parties should appeal to Nigerians for their votes rather than engage in activities that threaten their safety. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. The INEC chairman said violence could discourage voters from participating in elections, thereby compromising the democratic process. He said, “When participants cannot assemble, campaign or organise themselves, express their views freely, the political process is compromised long before election day. He cited Sections 95, 96 and 97 of the Electoral Act 2026, which provide guidelines on political rallies, prohibited campaign practices and threats of violence. He noted that Section 95 mandated state Commissioners of Police and the FCT Commissioner of Police to provide adequate security for political rallies and processions. The INEC chairman also warned political parties against organising, equipping or retaining security groups and political vanguards for campaigns. He said the police were obligated to protect lawful political activities rather than obstruct them, adding that parties and candidates must comply with notification requirements for rallies. Amupitan further disclosed that INEC would convene a security conference on Thursday, November 26, with the police, service chiefs and other members of the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security to address emerging threats and finalise security protocols for the 2027 elections. He also appealed to political parties to participate in the commission’s nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise scheduled for Saturday, November 28. He said the exercise would test the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, accreditation procedures and results transmission ahead of the general elections. The warning came amid growing concerns over political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections. The National Peace Committee recently disclosed that 26 states and the FCT recorded 109 breaches of the National Peace Accord between August 19 and October 27, 2026, with political violence and thuggery accounting for 33 incidents.
